# Minimal reproducers for CACHE_REVIEW.md D17 (fuzzer N2, CANCEL_LEAK) and D18 (fuzzer N3, stale values in t2).
# Source: probes/cache/src/optimus/graph/Repro17_18.scala. Build + run: probes/cache/run-repro.sh d17|d18 [reps]
# (compiles against probes/cache/classes + classes-hunter + the build classpath into probes/cache/classes-repro; same
# agents and opens as probes/cache/run.sh). JDK 21, default settings (XSFT on), no delay agent needed.
#
# Both are deterministic and single-threaded in their basic form; neither needs a race.
#   D17: 10/10 (basic) and 10/10 (mid-flight variant with a concurrent uncancelled waiter)
#   D18: 10/10 (TweakNode served) and 10/10 (DelayedCSProxyNode served, the node the fuzzer saw)
#
# =====================================================================================================================
# D17  An uncancelled request gets another request's OptimusCancellationException (by-name TweakNode poisoned)
# =====================================================================================================================
# Minimal shape (Repro17_18.d17Once):
#   root -> S1 = given(a := byName(b*4+134)) -> S2 = given(z := 1)        z unrelated, only makes S2 a real level
#   r1: inside a node on S2X = S2.withChildCancellationScope() (scope X):  X.cancel(); a.lookupAndGet  -> OCE (fine)
#   r2: a in S1 (no cancel scope anywhere)                                 -> OptimusCancellationException: D17-X
#   r3: a in S2                                                            -> OptimusCancellationException: D17-X
#
# Interleaving (file:line under optimus/platform/projects/core/src/main/scala/optimus):
#   1. r1 runs on S2X, a copy of S2 with a child cancel scope X: ScenarioStack.scala:843-845 -> withCancellationScopeRaw
#      :871-874 copies siParams only, so the copy's parent chain (S1, root) still carries NullCancellationScope.
#   2. a.lookupAndGet -> getNode -> TwkResolver walks S2X (no tweak) to S1 and finds the by-name tweak (cur = S1).
#      TwkResolver.scala:128 tweak.createNode(startSS = S2X, givenSS = S1, ...).
#   3. TweakNode.initialize, TweakNode.scala:175-177 (by-name; bindOnce is :179-180): scenarioStack = givenSS (S1,
#      NullCancellationScope) but computeSS = givenSS.parent.withSIParamsFrom(requestingSS); withSIParamsFrom
#      (ScenarioStack.scala:961-966) copies the requester's SIParams, which include its cancelScope X.
#      :191 attach(S1). TwkResolver.scala:132 caches the TweakNode under S1 (lookupAndInsert(tweakInfo, ...)).
#   4. TweakNode.run (TweakNode.scala:70-73) enqueues computeNode, which lives on computeSS (scope X).
#      X is cancelled, so OGSchedulerContext.java:855-856 runs computeNode.cancelInsteadOfRun (NodeTask.java:1419-1423),
#      completing it with X's cause; for a manual cancel that is the raw OptimusCancellationException
#      (CancellationScope.scala:55-56). (Mid-flight variant: the RHS is already running; its next child read is
#      enqueued on computeSS and is cancelled instead of run; same result.)
#   5. TweakNode.onChildCompleted -> completeFromNode(computeNode) (TweakNode.scala:84): the TweakNode, on S1 with
#      NullCancellationScope, is now done with X's exception, and it is in the cache.
#   6. r2/r3: a lookup from any stack whose cancel scope is NullCancellationScope finds the TweakNode;
#      NCSupport.isUsableWRTCancelScopeAndEnv fast path (NCSupport.java:202): equal cancelScopeAndEnvId -> reuse.
#      The HIDE_ON_DIFF_CS state bit (set, hideOnDiffCS=true below) is only consulted on the slow path.
#      Sticky: nothing invalidates it; every later request through a by-name/bindOnce resolution of a in S1 or
#      below fails.
#
# Why the fuzzer was intermittent and the earlier hand-written probes missed it: the requester must sit *below* the
# level holding the tweak (S2X walking up to S1). tweakcancelprobe/tweakcancelprobe2 used S1.withChildCancellationScope():
# the tweak is then found in the X-carrying copy itself (cur = S1X), givenSS carries X, and the poisoned TweakNode is
# correctly rejected by the slow path (control rows "requester=S1" below). In the fuzzer the timer must also fire after
# the requester started but before (or while) the TweakNode's RHS runs.
# Fuzzer trace (h2 seed 34 i2-a0-d0, request log from an instrumented scratch copy of CacheHunter):
#   REQ round=4 iter=2  node=11 path=2/6/11 key=p8[M,2] cancelScope=true cancelled=true  res=OptimusCancellationException
#   REQ round=4 iter=28 node=2  path=2      key=p8[M,2] cancelScope=false               res=OptimusCancellationException
#   p8 reads p0[M,2]; node 11 tweaks only p0[M,1], so p0[M,2] resolves to node 2's p0 := BYNAME(p0*4+134): the
#   TweakNode lands on node 2's stack (NullCancellationScope), its RHS on node 11's X. Exactly steps 1-6.
# Modes: BYNAME and BIND_ONCE leak; BIND (evaluateInCurrent) attaches the TweakNode to the requesting stack, no leak.
# Policy basic/default (XSFT) irrelevant.
#
# Classification: confirms D17 as new (not D1: no XS proxy involved).
# Candidate fix: run the RHS under the TweakNode's own cancel scope (computeSS = ...withSIParamsFrom(requestingSS)
# .withCancellationScopeRaw(givenSS.cancelScope)), or in onChildCompleted, if computeNode failed with a cancellation of
# a scope other than the TweakNode's, do not complete (re-run, or invalidate and complete without caching).
#
# $ probes/cache/run-repro.sh d17 10       (lines trimmed to the a-target rows; target=c rows are "ok": c is cancelled
#                                           before it reads a, so no TweakNode is created)
D17 LEAK mode=BYNAME    policy=default requester=S2 target=a r1(X)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r2(S1)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r3(S2)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  expected=154 rhsRuns=0 | node a@S1=TweakNode nodeCS=NullCancellationScope$ nodeCS.cancelled=false nodeSS==S1:true packedIdEq=true exc=OptimusCancellationException: D17-X hideOnDiffCS=true excIsX'sCause=true
D17 ok   mode=BYNAME    policy=default requester=S1 target=a r1(X)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r2(S1)=154  r3(S2)=154  expected=154 rhsRuns=1

D17 LEAK midflight mode=BIND_ONCE r1(X)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r2(none, concurrent)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r3(none, later)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  expected=154 rhsRuns=1
D17 ok   midflight mode=BIND      r1(X)=EXC OptimusCancellationException: D17-X  r2(none, concurrent)=154  r3(none, later)=154  expected=154 rhsRuns=2
D17 RATE midflight mode=BYNAME leaked=10/10
D17 RATE mode=BYNAME policy=default requester=S2 target=a leaked=10/10
#
# Fuzzer reruns this session: one h2 34 i2-a0-d0 8 -> 4/8; one h2 7 i4-a0-d1 2 -> CANCEL_LEAK in 1/2 (both runs FAIL on D4/F8).
#
# =====================================================================================================================
# D18  A cached TweakNode (or a CS proxy over one) answers the untweaked-key lookup after its `when` clause turns false
# =====================================================================================================================
# Minimal shape (Repro17_18.d18when): two trackers, no concurrency needed.
#   t0 (root): w := 8
#   t1 (consistent child of t0; concurrent works too): x := byName(b*10+g) when ((w >>> 3) & 1) == 1
#   1. evaluate x in t1        -> 57 (tweak applies)
#   2. t0: w := 0              (when clause now false; the oracle, and a fresh t1b with the same tweak, give 100)
#   3. evaluate x in t1        -> 57, expected 100. Permanent until something invalidates the TweakNode itself.
#
# Mechanism:
#   1. Step 1 resolves x in t1: TwkResolver finds the property tweak in t1 and runs the when clause in cur.parent
#      (TwkResolver.scala:157). The when clause's tweak dependency (w) is merged into the TwkResolver / tracking proxy
#      and passed on to the requesting node (TwkResolver.scala:76-89, :250), not into the TweakNode.
#      The by-name TweakNode is created, markAsTrackingValue'd and cached under t1's cache id
#      (TwkResolver.scala:128-132, lookupAndInsert(tweakInfo, tweakNode)). It records x and its RHS reads, not w.
#   2. w := 0 in t0 invalidates w's TTrack in t0 and, via children, t1's trackers: the requesters of x go, the
#      TweakNode stays valid (beforeInvalid=false below).
#   3. Next lookup of x in t1: the when clause re-runs (whenRunsOnFlipEval=1) and says "no tweak", so getNode looks up
#      the untweaked key: TwkResolver.scala:116-117 -> ScenarioStack.completeGetNode (ScenarioStack.scala:1077-1080) ->
#      lookupAndInsert(x.info, x@t1). In getIfPresentCore the cached TweakNode matches that key:
#        - value.equalsForCaching(key) (NodeCacheBase.java:176, PropertyNode.scala:307-313): TweakNode is a
#          ProxyPropertyNode, whose propertyInfo is srcNodeTemplate.propertyInfo and whose argsEquals delegates to
#          srcNodeTemplate (ProxyPropertyNode.scala:38-46). That is deliberate for delayed proxies
#          ("a cached proxy should be reused on lookups of its srcNodeTemplate", PropertyNode.scala:302-305), and
#          TweakNode inherits it;
#        - policy.matchesScenario (NodeCacheBase.java:179, NCPolicy.java:230): same cache id (t1's);
#        - isUsableWRTCancelScopeAndEnv: same scope or done with a usable result.
#      The direct probe below (UNodeCache.global.getIfPresent(x.info, untweaked x@t1)) returns the very TweakNode.
#   With two overlapping requesters of x in t1 under different cancel scopes (the queue's scope and a child scope,
#   as the fuzzer's cancellable evaluations make), the cached entry is a DelayedCSProxyNode over the TweakNode; it is
#   a ProxyPropertyNode too and aliases the same way. That is the node the fuzzer served (RAW line below).
#   Only the true -> false direction is affected: a base node never equals a TweakNode key (equalsForCaching is
#   asymmetric), so after false -> true the stale base node is merely latent (the fuzzer's STALE_LATENT p7 rows).
#
# Fuzzer instance (h3 seed 29 i2-a0-d0-w0 off=tags,xs; instrumented scratch copy of CacheHunter, STALEDIAG lines):
#   t2 (ph20): p7 := BYNAME(p1*5+998) when(arg%2==0 && bit0(p6[=,=]))      when read p6[e1,2] resolves in t1
#   t1 (ph21): p6[e1,2] := BIND_ONCE(p0+p5*2+702);  t1 (ph27): p0 := 831142  -> bit0 of p6[e1,2]@t1 flips to false
#   STALEDIAG   read p7[e1,2] curVal=761437037 served=4207187383 WRONG            (every stale node, p28/p32/p33/p35..)
#   STALEDIAG   RAW t2 p7[e1,2] in ss=11: DelayedCSProxyNode ss=11 inv=false v=4207187383 | in parent ss=13: TweakableLeaf v=761437037 | oracle=761437037
#   STALEDIAG   RAW t2 p6[e1,2] ... in parent ss=13: TweakNode v=534534090 (= t1's correct view; when clause false)
#   All stale nodes were computed in the same phase from the aliased p7 ("not in previous snapshot"), so they were never
#   valid-and-missed by invalidation: no TTrack hole.
#   The fuzzer's ingredients map directly: by-name (cached TweakNode), when clause with a read, the when input changed in
#   an ancestor tracker. The late consistent child t2 under the concurrent t1 is incidental: it is simply where seed 29
#   put the when-tweak whose input lives in a parent tracker. The toggles' "removed by batch/addasync/newchild" come from
#   the knob changing the whole action trajectory (an off action consumes fewer random numbers), not from causation.
#
# Classification: new. Not R4/D6 (no off-queue invalidation, no Invalid track: single thread, sequential updates,
# consistent child suffices); not D5 (no TweakExpander); not F3. Same family as F1 in that tweak-node identity in the
# cache collapses onto something it should not (here the untweaked key). Needs a mutable ancestor (a DependencyTracker),
# since otherwise a cache id fixes the when clause's inputs.
# Candidate fixes: make TweakNodes (and proxies over them) not equalsForCaching an untweaked key (e.g. TweakNode's
# argsEquals only matches TweakNodes of the same tweak, or cache TweakNodes under a distinct identity), or record the
# when-clause dependency on the TweakNode so the flip invalidates it (the CS proxy over it would then also need to
# follow).
#
# $ probes/cache/run-repro.sh d18 10       (columns trimmed)
D18 ok    rhs=CONST     r1=57 [cache probe for untweaked x@t1 after flip: TweakableLeaf] after-flip: x@t1=100 expected=100
D18 STALE rhs=BYNAME    conc=false proxy=false r1=57 [cache probe for untweaked x@t1 after flip: TweakNode same=true propertyInfo==x.info:true] [sanity w@t1=0 x@fresh-t1b=100] rawNodeBefore=TweakNode after-flip: x@t1=57 expected=100 rawNode=TweakNode sameAsBefore=true beforeInvalid=false whenRunsOnFlipEval=1 STALE
D18 STALE rhs=BIND_ONCE conc=false proxy=false ... cache probe: TweakNode same=true ... after-flip: x@t1=57 expected=100 STALE
D18 STALE rhs=BIND      conc=false proxy=false ... cache probe: TweakNode same=true ... after-flip: x@t1=57 expected=100 STALE
D18 STALE rhs=BYNAME conc=false proxy=true order=plainFirst r1=57 r2=57 [cache probe: DelayedCSProxyNode same=true] rawNodeBefore=DelayedCSProxyNode after-flip: x@t1=57 expected=100 STALE
D18 STALE rhs=BYNAME conc=false proxy=true order=childFirst  ... DelayedCSProxyNode ... x@t1=57 expected=100 STALE

#
# Fuzzer reruns this session: one h3 29 i2-a0-d0-w0 4 off=tags,xs -> 4/4 (twice).
# min h3 29 i2-a0-d0-w0 STALE_SERVED:UNEXPLAINED -> maxProps=41, removedBy=[byname,when,batch,canceleval] (trajectory
# effects as above; with off=tags,xs,canceleval it still fails 4/4).
